headline: Man Builds Little Free Library, Fills It Entirely With Copies of Same Book
summary: Maple Street installation contains 14 copies of 'Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance,' owner calls it 'curated experience.'
content:
When retired engineer Douglas Pratt installed a Little Free Library in front of his Maple Street home last month, neighbors were pleased. When they discovered it contained 14 identical copies of 'Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance,' they were confused.

"It's not a random collection," Pratt, 68, explained. "It's a curated experience. This book changed my life in 1982, and I believe it could change other people's lives too. So I'm giving them every opportunity."

The hand-built wooden structure, painted a cheerful blue and properly registered with the Little Free Library organization, adheres to the program's "take a book, leave a book" philosophy—with a twist. A small sign inside reads: "Take a book. Leave any book. But consider: have you read THIS book?"

Neighbors have had mixed reactions.

"I already own a copy," said resident Maria Santos. "I took one anyway, just to see if he'd notice. He did. He put another one in the same day. I don't know where he's getting them."

Pratt confirmed that he has an "ongoing arrangement" with several used bookstores and monitors online listings. "I've acquired probably 200 copies over the years," he said. "I always knew they'd have a purpose."

The library has successfully distributed approximately 23 copies since opening, though Pratt notes that several have been returned, "presumably by people who weren't ready for it."

When asked if he would ever consider stocking different titles, Pratt was thoughtful. "Maybe someday," he said. "But I want to fully explore what happens when an entire community reads the same book. We're only a month in. The data is still coming in."

He has started a notebook to track observations. It currently contains the entry: "Mrs. Patterson took copy #7. Saw her at grocery store. She avoided eye contact. Progress?"
author: Janet Reeves, Community Correspondent
